method: Two-point measurement against the CLI's own accounting. A payload of known char length is injected via --append-system-prompt; cache_creation_input_tokens is read from --output-format json and the no-payload baseline subtracted. Uses the real production tokenizer; no third-party tokenizer is involved.
linearity_check: 20k java predicts 17356 tokens at 40k; measured 16566 (-4.6%). Deviation is composition, not nonlinearity: the second 20k is IndexWriter.java, which is javadoc-heavy English (less dense than code).
finding: grep output is 1.84 chars/token vs 2.35 for Java source - it is ~25% denser per character because file paths, colons and line numbers fragment into many tokens. Attributing grep output at a source-code ratio would UNDERCOUNT the cost of the search arm by about a quarter.
